title: Local colimit cones give a restriction equivalence on coherent cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe and containing universes for functor categories. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small ordinary category, and $F:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/K}$ a functor, where an object of $\mathrm{sSet}_{/K}$ is a simplicial map $\pi_a:K_a\to K$ and a morphism is a simplicial map commuting with the maps to $K$. Define a simplicial set $K_F$ as follows. An $n$-simplex consists of a cut $-1\leq i\leq n$, a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K$ when $i\geq0$, a chain $a_{i+1}\to\cdots\to a_n$ in $I$ when $i<n$, and compatible lifts $\sigma_j:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K_{a_j}$ for $j>i$, with $\pi_{a_j}\sigma_j=\sigma$ and $F(a_j\to a_k)\sigma_j=\sigma_k$. When $i=-1$ the lower block and lifts are empty, so the simplex is just the chain in $N(I)$; when $i=n$ the upper block is empty, so it is just $\sigma\in K_n$. Operators restrict or repeat the two ordered blocks, restrict the lower simplices, and compose or repeat the upper arrows; when one block disappears, retain the pure simplex in the other block. Thus $K$ and $N(I)$ are disjoint simplicial subsets of $K_F$. The map $\iota_a:K_a^{\triangleright}\to K_F$ uses $\pi_a$ on its base and the constant upper chain at $a$, carrying its new cone vertex to the vertex $a$ of $N(I)$. Here $X^{\triangleright}=X\star\Delta^0$ is the join whose simplices are simplices of $X$, constant simplices at a new last vertex, and ordered concatenations of those two kinds. Although $\iota_a$ need not be injective, it is a specified simplicial map.

Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory, $p:K\to\mathcal E$ a diagram, and $q:K_F\to\mathcal E$ an extension of $p$. Suppose that, for every $a\in I$, the cocone $q\iota_a:K_a^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ is colimiting for $p\pi_a$. Then for every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of spaces
$$ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_F,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_{K_F}T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT). $$
It is natural in $T$ and compatible with coherent postcomposition of cocones. No existence of other colimits in $\mathcal E$, no directedness of $I$, and no injectivity of the maps $K_a\to K$ are assumed. A join cocone here is read as a coherent transformation by the map $K_a\times\Delta^1\to K_a^{\triangleright}$ which retains the initial vertices labelled $0$ and sends the final vertices labelled $1$ to the new cone vertex.

proof.text: The degreewise block formula in the statement defines a simplicial set. Restricting or repeating vertices in the lower simplex and composing or repeating arrows in the upper chain preserves the compatibility equations; when a block disappears, the stated pure simplex is obtained. Hence the inclusions of K and N(I) are simplicial, and the maps iota_a from the right joins K_a^{triangleright} are simplicial. This is a direct verification from the ordered join and coherent-diagram conventions.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1 and Remark 4.2.3.2, pp. 248-249; degreewise definition of the collage.

proof.text:
Use the relative skeletal cells of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to order the nondegenerate simplices of $N(I)$ dimension by dimension, well-ordering each small set of cells. Let $Y_0=\varnothing$, attach one simplex along its entire boundary at each successor, and take unions at limits. For $Y\subseteq N(I)$ let $A(Y)\subseteq K_F$ contain $K$ and exactly those remaining simplices whose upper block belongs to $Y$. Put $A_\alpha=A(Y_\alpha)$ and $q_\alpha=q|_{A_\alpha}$. Thus $A_0=K$ and the final union is $K_F$. If the attached simplex is $\sigma=(a_0\to\cdots\to a_n)$, the square attaching $A_\alpha$ to $A_{\alpha+1}$ is the pushout of
$$K_{a_0}\star\partial\Delta^n\longrightarrow K_{a_0}\star\Delta^n.$$
Here $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$ and $L\star\varnothing=L$. The attaching map on the pure lower block is $\pi_{a_0}$; on a mixed simplex with lower lift $u$ and upper face beginning at $a_j$, its first lift is $F(a_0\to a_j)u$, followed by its images along that face. To check the pushout degreewise, a simplex not already in $A_\alpha$ has upper block a degeneracy of the newly attached nondegenerate $\sigma$, with its surjection onto $[n]$. Its first upper vertex is therefore $a_0$, and its lower lift in $K_{a_0}$ uniquely supplies the remaining data. The other simplices of the attaching join have upper block in the boundary or are pure lower simplices, so are identified with the old part. This proves the claimed pushout even when $\pi_{a_0}$ is not injective.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, filtration by simplices of N(I) and the displayed join pushout, pp.249-250; degreewise verification added.

proof.text:
We first give the boundary argument needed at a successor. For a quasicategory $Q$ and $s:\Delta^n\to Q$ with $s(0)$ initial, write $J_s$ for the join cocone quasicategory defined in [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], and write $s_\partial=s|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. A boundary lifting problem of dimension $m\geq0$ for $J_s\to J_{s_\partial}$ is, by that degreewise definition, precisely a map into $Q$ on
$$(\partial\Delta^n\star\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^n\star\partial\Delta^m)=\partial\Delta^{n+m+1}.$$
Its first vertex is $s(0)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $Q\to\Delta^0$: its relative-initial condition at $s(0)$ is exactly initiality, since every target mapping space is a point. This map is an inner fibration because $Q$ is a quasicategory. The boundary dimension $n+m+1$ is positive, including $n=m=0$, so the lemma gives the desired filler with the entire prescribed boundary fixed. Hence $J_s\to J_{s_\partial}$ has the right lifting property for every boundary inclusion, including dimension zero, and is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The case $n=0$ reads $J_{s(0)}\to Q$ because the join cocone category of the empty diagram is $Q$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.3.3, pp.249-250; its double-join boundary calculation is expanded, including dimension zero.

proof.text:
For a successor cell $\sigma=(a_0\to\cdots\to a_n)$ set $L=K_{a_0}$, $b=p\pi_{a_0}$ and $Q=J_b$. The join-slice comparison [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] makes $Q$ a quasicategory and makes the vertex represented by $q\iota_{a_0}$ initial, because its associated coherent cocone is colimiting by hypothesis. Restriction of $q$ to the attaching join $L\star\Delta^n$ is exactly a simplex $s:\Delta^n\to Q$. Its first vertex is that local cocone, including when $n=0$. The pushout of step 2 identifies the restriction map
$$J_{q_{\alpha+1}}\longrightarrow J_{q_\alpha}$$
with the pullback of $J_s\to J_{s_\partial}$ along restriction of an old cocone to $L\star\partial\Delta^n$. Explicitly an $m$-simplex on the new piece is a map $(L\star\Delta^n)\star\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ fixed on $L\star\Delta^n$; associating the ordered three blocks identifies it with $\Delta^n\star\Delta^m\to J_b$ fixed on $s$. On its boundary this is precisely the old-piece restriction. The joins associate because each simplex is an ordered concatenation of the same three blocks, with the same operators. The join operation with a fixed right factor preserves this nonempty pushout: degreewise its pure right simplices are identified once and its remaining summands preserve the set pushout. Thus this is an identity of the whole simplicial pullback, not just of its vertices. Step 3 proves the pulled-back map is a trivial Kan fibration: a boundary lifting problem in the pullback is a problem for that map with its old-piece coordinate already prescribed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, successor pullback of the cocone restriction of Lemma 4.2.3.3, p.250; all block identifications made explicit.

proof.text: At a limit ordinal $\lambda$, a map $A_\lambda\star\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ is exactly a compatible family of maps $A_\alpha\star\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ for $\alpha<\lambda$: the domain is the union degreewise, with its pure right factor already shared. It follows that $J_{q_\lambda}=\varprojlim_{\alpha<\lambda}J_{q_\alpha}$ as simplicial sets. To fill a boundary square for the final restriction $J_q\to J_p$, start with its given $\Delta^m$-simplex in $J_p$. Inductively lift that simplex along every successor map of step 4, using the prescribed restriction of the original $\partial\Delta^m$-simplex. At limits the previously chosen compatible lifts define their union. This constructs a lift of the entire $\Delta^m$ keeping its boundary fixed. It works for $m=0$ as well: the boundary is empty and each successor still has its dimension-zero filler. Thus the final restriction has all boundary lifts, and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes $J_q\to J_p$ a trivial Kan fibration. This argument uses actual lifts, not an inference that an ordinary inverse limit of arbitrary weak equivalences is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, limit ordinal and final transfinite tower, pp.250-251; recursive boundary lifts written out.

proof.text:
All maps $J_{q_\beta}\to J_{q_\alpha}$ retain the apex, since they restrict only the diagram block of the ordered join. Pull back the final trivial Kan fibration along $J_p\times_{\mathcal E}\{T\}\to J_p$; its source is $J_q\times_{\mathcal E}\{T\}$. A boundary lift of this pullback keeps the prescribed $J_p$ coordinate, so it keeps its constant apex $T$ in every degree. The pullback is therefore again a trivial Kan fibration and a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The fixed-apex clause of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] gives natural equivalences from its two Kan complexes to
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_F,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_{K_F}T),\qquad \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT).$$
Naturality with respect to shape restriction identifies the intervening map with the actual restriction in the statement, so it too is a weak equivalence. The comparisons are also natural in the apex and preserve coherent postcomposition by the same cited statement. Restriction of join data commutes exactly with precomposition on the diagram block; consequently its coherent-transformation version is natural in $T$ and compatible with coherent postcomposition. The filler choices above prove that this specified map is an equivalence and are not used to define it.

lean.note: Constructs the specified K_F as a coequalizer of upper-chain join generators, with every simplex-operator identification and pure lower gluing along π. The local hypothesis is the absolute-colimit specialization over the terminal simplicial set, not the identity map. The conclusion is the actual mapping-space restriction at each apex and its coherent constant-diagram square. The helpers belong to the decomposition notion introduced by this node; no independent new notion or postponed construction theorem is introduced.
